title: Buffered I/O
description:
Model how the I/O manager copies buffers for `METHOD_BUFFERED`.

```
user input "hello" (5), output buffer 16
system buffer: 16 bytes, input copied in
driver writes "HELLO!" (6) and sets Information = 6
I/O manager copies 6 bytes back to the user's output
driver claims Information = 20 -> refused (more than the output buffer)
```
hints: Because input and output share one buffer, read everything you need from the input before writing output (lesson 2.04).
Information too large is the bug where a driver leaks kernel memory to user mode.
requirements: The system buffer is `max(inLength, outLength)` bytes; the input is copied in first.
The driver reads input and writes output in the same buffer.
Copying back uses `Information`, which must not exceed the output length.
stretch: Model `METHOD_OUT_DIRECT` too, where the output is the user's own pages locked in memory.
